claims.text: Malassezia causes the rash only in its filamentous (hyphal) form
claims.quote: is a dimorphic yeast-like fungus. It causes PV only in its pathogenic, filamentous (hyphal) form.

claims.text: Malassezia genus has 19 species and is part of the healthy skin microbiome
claims.quote: currently comprising 19 species, remains an integral component of the healthy skin microbiome

claims.text: patches mainly on trunk, neck, upper arms
claims.quote: PV is characterised by scaly hypopigmented or hyperpigmented patches, primarily affecting the upper trunk, neck, and upper arms.

claims.text: Wood lamp: only about one third of lesions fluoresce; showering may wash away chromophores
claims.quote: it has been shown that only one third of the PV lesions display fluorescence with Wood’s lamp []. One of the factors seemingly responsible for this number could be washing out the chromophores with a shower/bath

claims.text: first-line treatment is topical, including selenium sulfide 2.5%
claims.quote: Topical therapies are the primary treatment for PV, encompassing non-specific antifungal agents like sulphur with salicylic acid, selenium sulphide 2.5%, and zinc pyrithione.

claims.text: prolonged topical prophylaxis should be considered in recurrent cases, warmer humid months
claims.quote: Prolonged prophylaxis with topical agents should be considered in recurrent cases, especially during warmer and more humid months.

claims.text: prevalence up to 50% tropical, 1-4% moderate, 1% cold climates
claims.quote: The prevalence of PV reaches up to 50% in tropical regions, whereas it is estimated to be around 1–4% and 1% in moderate and cold climates, respectively

claims.text: lipid-dependent yeast lives in sebum-rich areas (chest, upper back, face, scalp)
claims.quote: Sebaceous areas of the human skin, including the scalp, face, chest, and upper back, remain a habitat for thegenus due to the abundance of a lipid nutrient source

claims.text: most often develops in adolescents and young adults because of increased sebum
claims.quote: it most often develops in adolescents and young adults due to increased sebum production by the sebaceous glands

claims.text: predisposing factors: hot humid environment, sweating, oily emollients, seborrhea, pregnancy, oral contraceptives, corticosteroids, malnutrition, poor health, genetics; heat favors filamentous conversion
claims.quote: conversion from the yeast-like form include a hot and humid environment, hyperhidrosis, the application of oily emollients, using protective face masks, seborrhoea, endocrine and neuropathic disorders, pregnancy, the use of oral contraceptives and corticosteroids, malnutrition, poor general health

claims.text: genetic predisposition is also listed
claims.quote: the use of oral contraceptives and corticosteroids, malnutrition, poor general health, and genetic predisposition

claims.text: organism interacts with melanocytes to produce discolored patches
claims.quote: the fungus has a potential to produce hypo- or hyperpigmented patches by interacting with melanocytes

claims.text: azelaic acid from Malassezia inhibits tyrosinase (lighter patches)
claims.quote: Depigmented lesions develop through enzymatic inhibition of melanocyte tyrosinase activity by azelaic acid produced by the microorganism.

claims.text: lipid-like material may act as a physical sunscreen
claims.quote: lipid-like material accumulates in the stratum corneum, acting as a physical sunscreen and protecting from ultraviolet light, further enhancing hypopigmentation.

claims.text: pityriacitrin turned out to have very weak sun-protective properties
claims.quote: One of the substances suspected of this photo-protective action was pityriacitrin [], yet its sun-protective properties were proven to be very weak

claims.text: lighter patches more visible in darker skin
claims.quote: The effects of enzymatic depigmentation tend to be more visible in darker phototypes.

claims.text: darker patches more common in lighter skin tones
claims.quote: Hyperpigmented lesions are, in turn, more common in lighter skin tones

claims.text: location: back, shoulders, neck, chest; less often abdomen, upper arms, thighs
claims.quote: The disorder commonly affects seborrheic areas: back and shoulder girdle, neck, chest, and less frequently abdomen, upper arms, and thighs

claims.text: facial involvement uncommon, reported particularly in children (symptoms list, clinical forms, FAQ)
claims.quote: Facial involvement is uncommon and has been reported particularly in children

claims.text: itching often absent; mild itch worse with warmth, humidity, sweating
claims.quote: The disease is often asymptomatic, although some patients may report mild pruritus that may intensify with warmth and high humidity (e.g., after sweating)

claims.text: classical form: round macules with delicate scale that may merge
claims.quote: hyper- or hypopigmented, poorly to well-delineated, roundish macules covered with delicate translucent scales. Skin lesions may have a tendency towards becoming confluent.

claims.text: follicular form on chest and back; spots around follicles that may merge
claims.quote: Folliculocentric PV predominantly affects the chest and back regions. This form impacts the hair follicles, giving rise to asymptomatic, hypo- or hyperpigmented macules. These macules are exclusively located around the follicles and may occasionally merge

claims.text: other variants: inverse, atrophying, papular, confetti-like
claims.quote: a variant termed “tinea InVersicolor” or “Inverse PV”. ... Atrophying PV, another distinct form ... The papular form of PV ... The confetti-like subtype

claims.text: diagnosis usually from clinical appearance alone
claims.quote: Classical PV rarely requires any work-up other than clinical examination.

claims.text: KOH gives no stain; methylene green, PAS or blue ink improve visualization
claims.quote: As adding KOH provides no stain, methylene green, periodic acid–Schiff (PAS; with methylene green or fuchsin), or simply common blue ink can be used for better visualisation

claims.text: sample the periphery; darker lesions contain more hyphae and spores
claims.quote: As the highest concentration of fungi is noted at the lesion’s periphery [,], we recommend taking the sample from this area ... Hyperpigmented lesions tend to contain more hyphae and spores than the hypopigmented ones

claims.text: KOH microscopy is not 100% sensitive
claims.quote: direct microscopic examination with KOH does not provide 100% sensitivity

claims.text: Wood lamp peak wavelength 365 nm
claims.quote: Wood’s light is an ultraviolet light (UV) emitter (wavelength range: 320–450 nm; peak wavelength: 365 nm).

claims.text: culture not recommended; olive-oil media, 1 to 4 weeks incubation
claims.quote: Microbiological culture in PV is not recommended []. The process is difficult for the required use of synthetic mycological media enriched with olive oil, and 1–4 weeks of incubation at 32 °C

claims.text: topical is treatment of choice; oral second-line for extensive, severe, unresponsive or recurrent disease
claims.quote: Topical therapy is the treatment of choice for PV ... Oral medications are utilised as a second-line treatment for extensive, severe, unresponsive, or recurrent disease.

claims.text: reviews also describe 2-week selenium sulfide courses
claims.quote: Selenium sulphide lotion should be applied once daily (for 10 min), whereas the treatment duration should be 2 weeks.

claims.text: whole-body antifungal washes might limit recurrence but poorly supported
claims.quote: The whole-body application of antifungal shampoos or soaps with selenium sulphide, zinc pyrithione, ketoconazole, and terbinafine might limit the recurrence rate []. Nevertheless, it is worth underlining that such management is still poorly supported with the literature.

claims.text: topical treatment should also cover the scalp, a major reservoir
claims.quote: every topical therapy should also target the scalp, a major reservoir of the fungus

claims.text: itraconazole and fluconazole are the preferred oral options
claims.quote: Itraconazole and fluconazole are preferred, whereas oral ketoconazole is no longer recommended, due to its unfavourable safety profile

claims.text: topical agents: better safety profile, fewer interactions, lower cost
claims.quote: they have a better safety profile, with a lower incidence of adverse effects (local irritation and contact allergy being the most prevalent, especially with selenium sulphide), fewer drug interactions, and lower costs compared to systemic treatment

claims.text: oral prophylaxis with itraconazole or fluconazole is a practical alternative if topical agents fail
claims.quote: Prophylactic use of oral antifungal agents (viz., itraconazole or fluconazole) remains a practical alternative, especially if topical agents fail to eliminate the infection

claims.text: washing and ironing clothes; clothing can be a reservoir
claims.quote: Additional measures include washing and ironing the clothes, as these can serve as a reservoir

claims.text: higher incidence in immunocompromised people and in diabetes or obesity
claims.quote: Higher incidence has been noted in physically active individuals, patients suffering from diabetes and obesity, and immunocompromised individuals.

claims.text: FAQ: topical treatment works well for most limited disease
claims.quote: Treatment response is excellent in the majority of PV cases treated with topical agents only.
